memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But whenever raw flesh appears on them, they will be unclean. When the priest sees the raw flesh, he shall pronounce them unclean. The raw flesh is unclean; they have a defiling skin disease. If the raw flesh changes and turns white, they must go to the priest. The priest is to examine them, and if the sores have turned white, the priest shall pronounce the affected person clean; then they will be clean." - Lev 13:14-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The previous verses gave that surprising verdict: fully covered, and therefore clean. Now comes the exception. If raw flesh appears anywhere on that body, the verdict reverses immediately.

One patch. That is all it took.

Follow the thought from yesterday. Complete honesty before God brings us into grace. But there is a way of appearing to surrender everything while quietly keeping one area back — one relationship we will not release, one grudge we will not surrender, one part of our finances or our future that we have decided is not up for discussion.

We can be very devout about ninety-nine percent. Ananias and Sapphira brought a genuine gift; their sin was pretending it was everything (Acts 5:1-4). The rich young ruler kept every commandment he could name, and walked away sad over one thing (Mark 10:21-22).

But look at how the passage ends. If the raw flesh changes and turns white, he shall pronounce them clean. The door does not close. The person could come back. A reversed verdict was not the final word.

Whatever you have been holding back, it is not too late to open your hand.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What is the one area you have quietly marked "not up for discussion" with God?
2. Why does that particular thing feel too costly to surrender?
3. What small step of surrender could you take this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I have offered You much while holding one thing back. You know exactly what it is. Give me the trust to open my hand and let You have all of me. Amen.
